steps.title: Piedmont
steps.body: Nebbiolo's heart is the Langhe and Roero, around Alba, in Piedmont. Barolo and Barbaresco are its great wines. Roero, across the Tanaro river, makes lighter, more perfumed Nebbiolo on sandy soils. Langhe Nebbiolo and Nebbiolo d'Alba are more affordable regional wines.

steps.title: Northern Piedmont and Lombardy
steps.body: In northern Piedmont, Nebbiolo is called Spanna and grows in Gattinara, Ghemme, Boca and Lessona, on volcanic and acidic soils, giving fresher, more mineral wines. In Lombardy's Valtellina, it's called Chiavennasca and grows on steep Alpine terraces. Valle d'Aosta's Donnas also uses it.

steps.prompt: Match each name or place to Nebbiolo.
steps.explanation: Nebbiolo has several homes in northern Italy.

steps.title: Hard to transplant
steps.body: Nebbiolo is very site-specific: it needs warm, sunny slopes, often south-facing, and calcareous marl to show its best. Plantings in California, Australia and Argentina exist, but few match Piedmont. It's one of the least travelled great grapes.

steps.prompt: What is Nebbiolo called in Valtellina?
steps.explanation: Chiavennasca grows on Valtellina's steep Alpine terraces.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Nebbiolo's heart is the Langhe and Roero
It's Spanna in northern Piedmont and Chiavennasca in Valtellina
It's very site-specific and rarely succeeds abroad
